security_audit.summary: The three static findings are false positives caused by general security-audit terminology and safety guidance in SKILL.md. No prompt injection, credential exfiltration, executable code, or unauthorized command behavior was found in the reviewed skill file. One medium semantic risk remains because the skill lists social engineering as a penetration testing capability.

remediation.issue: The skill lists social engineering as a penetration testing capability.
remediation.suggestion: Limit this capability to consent-based simulations and add explicit refusal language for phishing, impersonation, credential harvesting, or targeting real people.

finding_verdicts.reason: Line 38 instructs users to protect sensitive data and avoid exposing secrets in reports. This is defensive reporting guidance, not system reconnaissance.
Line 72 describes IAST as a security testing method in a capabilities list. It does not instruct the agent to enumerate host systems or collect environment details.
Lines 17-18 describe authorized SDLC reviews and vulnerability mitigation planning. The surrounding guidance requires scope approval, so this is not network reconnaissance.

content.value_statement: Security teams need structured reviews that connect vulnerabilities to business risk. This skill guides authorized audits, threat modeling, compliance checks, and remediation planning.
actual_capabilities: Plan authorized security audits with scope, assets, and compliance requirements.
Review DevSecOps pipelines for SAST, DAST, dependency scanning, and policy controls.
Guide threat modeling for applications, APIs, cloud systems, and Kubernetes deployments.
Prioritize vulnerabilities by severity, business impact, and remediation effort.
Prepare security documentation for incident response, governance, and compliance readiness.
limitations: Does not replace legal advice or formal compliance certification.
Requires clear authorization before any live security testing.
Does not guarantee complete vulnerability discovery.
Needs accurate system context, architecture details, and test boundaries.

use_cases.title: Prepare a Product Security Review
use_cases.description: Assess application architecture, authentication, authorization, data protection, and dependency risk before release.

use_cases.title: Improve DevSecOps Controls
use_cases.description: Map pipeline security checks to practical controls for scanning, policy enforcement, and remediation tracking.

use_cases.title: Organize Compliance Readiness
use_cases.description: Translate framework requirements into evidence requests, control gaps, and practical remediation steps.

prompt_templates.title: Start a Security Review
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this application for security risks. Ask for missing scope, assets, data types, and compliance requirements before giving findings.

prompt_templates.title: Prioritize Existing Findings
prompt_templates.prompt: Group these vulnerability findings by severity, business impact, exploit likelihood, and remediation order. Include clear owner actions.

prompt_templates.title: Threat Model an Architecture
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a threat model for this architecture using trust boundaries, assets, entry points, abuse cases, and mitigations.

prompt_templates.title: Design a DevSecOps Program
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a DevSecOps roadmap for this team. Include pipeline controls, policy gates, evidence collection, metrics, and incident response integration.

output_examples.input: Audit our API authentication and authorization design before launch.
output: Defines assets, trust boundaries, user roles, and sensitive operations.
Identifies access control gaps, token risks, and session handling issues.
Ranks fixes by business impact and release readiness.

output_examples.input: Review our CI/CD security controls for compliance readiness.
output: Maps pipeline stages to required security checks and evidence.
Highlights missing dependency, secret, container, and policy controls.
Recommends owners, timelines, and validation steps.

output_examples.input: Create an incident response plan for a cloud application.
output: Defines detection signals, escalation paths, containment actions, and recovery steps.
Lists evidence to preserve for investigation and reporting.
Connects response tasks to responsible teams.

best_practices: Confirm authorization, scope, and test boundaries before reviewing security controls.
Ask for architecture, data flow, identity, deployment, and compliance context.
Report findings with evidence, impact, priority, remediation, and validation steps.
anti_patterns: Using the skill for systems without permission or a defined testing scope.
Treating automated scan output as complete without manual validation.
Publishing sensitive data, secrets, or exploit details in reports.

faq.question: Can this skill run a full penetration test?
faq.answer: It can help plan and document authorized testing, but it does not replace a qualified penetration testing engagement.

faq.question: Does this skill support compliance audits?
faq.answer: It supports readiness work for frameworks such as SOC 2, HIPAA, GDPR, PCI-DSS, ISO 27001, and NIST.

faq.question: What inputs improve the audit quality?
faq.answer: Architecture diagrams, data flows, threat models, scan results, access models, cloud details, and compliance goals improve the output.

faq.question: Can it prioritize vulnerabilities?
faq.answer: Yes. It can rank issues by severity, exploit likelihood, business impact, exposure, and remediation effort.

faq.question: Is it safe for production systems?
faq.answer: Use it for planning and review. Any live testing needs written approval, defined scope, and production safety controls.

faq.question: Which tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report marks it compatible with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
